questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I dreamed of living in an other European country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was the most challenging semester I have ever tried, both academic and social. That being said, I learned a whole lot about myself and got to have an experience I will never forget.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I got most of the information I needed in the introduction week.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, but I wasn't expecting it, although I know some people had help finding housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Make sure to be there for the introduction week - a lot of crucial information.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very hard to find housing. I had nothing when I arrived, so I had to find it on my own, since the university could not give me any.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I can recommend two websides: livinfrance and studently
They are both great websides to find a place to stay before you arrive. If you want to live away from campus, make sure to begin looking in advance. Keep away from the Bagatelle area. It is not nice to live there.

I found my accommodation through Leboncoin, but I cannot recommend that since it is very easy to be scammed, and you need a French SIM card to register.
Furthermore, you must always lie about the fact that you are going to stay for a year and not a semester. They will not accept you if you tell them the truth. By French law you can always cancel your rent a month before you leave, so you will not be in any trouble.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's hard, I wish you best of luck!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy to register, but I only had the catalogue from last year, so some of the courses were removed and new ones were added. So, keep an eye out for changes. Was quite easy to mend your LA.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You need an adresse to register, but besides that it was quite easy.
We did not have acces to the intra web for some time but it all worked out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were in general really kind at the international office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I signed up for, although I had to change my LA after arrival because some courses were removed and others added.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have an adresse in Toulouse, and make sure that University of Copenhagen know about you changes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had 12 courses, it was completely madness. The level was the same as what I was used to, but the work burden was a lot bigger since I had 12 courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
If you want to make it a little bit easier for yourself, take courses at BA level or at TSM. They tend to be a bit easier. I took only MA courses at TSE and it was way more work than I had anticipated. Can recommend
Project Management.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar, but weird with the TP's since it was madetory to be there.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Game theory, 
Macroeconomics, 
Theory of Incentives, 
Environmental Economics, 
Markov Chains and Applications, 
Evolution of Economic Behavior, 
Experimental Economics, 
Understanding Real World Organizations, 
Political economy, 
Project management, 
R programming, 
Markets and Incentives : historical-critical perspective

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Markets and Incentives : historical-critical perspective was a really interesting course.
Political Economy was nice as well but the work burden was big.
I can also recommend experimental economics if you are into that field.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Could not end my subscription at my phone company.
Avoid for all cost the company "Free".

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating and drinkring out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I loved the city, it was vibrant with life! Can especially recommend a wine bar called: Nabuchodonosor
Cheap and good wine (if you like nature wine)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of sports activities. I did unfortunately not participate, but I would recommend doing it! Besides that, a lot of the social activities were in French, so a bit difficult to be a part of if you don't speak French.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely do sports as it is a great way to learn meet French people. I would also check out the community/jazz house "Maison Blanche" - A really cool place!
Can also recommend to go to the Cafe des Langues if you want to meet some other Erasmus people. A nice way getting to know other people than those from economics.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went hiking a lot in the Pyrenees! You can take a train from Toulouse all the way to the height of 2.500m. Go to the station Andorra L'Hopital. Plenty of good routes there. Can also highly recommend going to Albi and Bordeaux, some great places to check out!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The most difficult part was of course the language, but besides that it was a lot like Denmark, even though the work ethics is quite different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sports! And go to the BDE things if you'd like to get to know some people. The best thing you can do is to learn French! Even a little French gets you a far way, so can highly recommend to do some French courses before you go abroad.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People have no respect for queues, so you have to get used to that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the relaxed atmosphere of the city. You can really feel that you're close to the Mediterranean ocean, so everything is a little more loose than in Paris.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't panic.
Find a place to stay before you arrive.
Make sure that your courses are compatible with those of university of Copenhagen.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will have to work hard through out the whole semester if you want to pass the final exams. The work burden is insane at TSE, so it is not possible to study for all the exams in the exam season.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning a new language, people and getting through the semester.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The 12 different courses I had at the same time. Had some breakdowns throughout my exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Rememeber to have fun!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
